sections.heading: Difference between validating and leading
paragraphs: Per the file, the fundamental difference between (per the file) the pipelines is when (per the file) the PoH is present. Per the file, in a leader, we process txs, removing bad ones, and (per the file) then tag the result (per the file) with a PoH hash. Per the file, in the node, we verify that hash, (per the file) peel it off, and process the txs in exactly the same way. Per the file, the only difference is that if a node sees a bad tx, it can't simply remove (per the file) it like the leader does, (per the file) because that would cause the (per the file) PoH hash to change. Per the file, instead, it rejects the whole block. Per the file, the other difference between (per the file) the pipelines is what happens _after_ banking.

Per the file, the leader broadcasts entries to downstream nodes whereas the node will have already done (per the file) that in RetransmitStage, which (per the file) is a confirmation time optimization. Per the file, the validation pipeline, on (per the file) the other hand, has one last step. Per the file, any time it finishes (per the file) processing a block, it (per the file) needs to weigh any (per the file) forks it's observing, possibly (per the file) cast a vote, and if (per the file) so, reset its PoH hash (per the file) to the block hash it (per the file) just voted on.
